headline: 24 Bangladeshis injured, 2 killed in Houthi missile attack on Riyadh airport
summary: The identities of 24 Bangladeshis injured and two killed in a Houthi missile attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh have been confirmed. The Bangladesh Embassy is ensuring treatment for the affected and assisting stranded passengers.
details: The identities of 24 Bangladeshis injured in a missile attack by Yemen’s Houthi group on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh have been confirmed. This is in addition to the two Bangladeshis who were killed in the incident.
The attack, which occurred around 3:15 PM on Saturday, involved a missile exploding over Terminal 3. Overall, the incident killed 12 people of different nationalities and injured 309 others.
Among the casualties, two Bangladeshis were killed, and 24 were injured. The injured include 11 expatriate workers and 13 Umrah visa holders, all now receiving medical attention.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh is maintaining round-the-clock contact with hospital authorities to ensure proper treatment for those affected. The Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment confirmed these efforts.
One of the deceased was Md Shahed Ahmed from Bogura, a plumber returning to Jeddah via Riyadh. The other victim was Md Nasrullah Badarpuri from Cumilla, an Umrah visa holder in transit to Jeddah.

The 24 injured Bangladeshis are currently undergoing treatment at 11 hospitals across Riyadh, including King Abdullah Hospital and National Guard Hospital. Embassy representatives have visited some patients, noting stable conditions for several.

Following the attack, the Bangladesh Embassy also stepped in to assist approximately 500 Bangladeshi passengers stranded at the airport and on domestic routes. Accommodation was arranged for 100 passengers at various hotels and university dormitories.

Furthermore, 67 Umrah pilgrims were sent to Jeddah by special buses, and arrangements were made for around 400 passengers of a cancelled Saudia Airlines flight to return to Bangladesh via Dammam. Two workers bound for Bahrain were also assisted.

This incident marked another in a series of attacks; the Houthis had launched a previous strike the day before, killing 13. They also launched another attack on Riyadh airport on Sunday, causing a fire and prompting warnings to airlines and passengers.

headline_marked: [[Two retired army officers arrested]] in Dhaka under Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Security Acts
headline: Two retired army officers arrested in Dhaka under Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Security Acts
summary: Lt Col (retd) Debashish Kumar Barua and Lt (retd) Gulshan Ara were apprehended in separate late-night raids across the capital, confirmed by Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch.
details: Two retired army officers, Lt Col (retd) Debashish Kumar Barua and Lt (retd) Gulshan Ara, were arrested in Dhaka late last night.
The arrests were made in connection with cases filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act and the Cyber Security Act.
They were apprehended in separate raids conducted at different locations within the capital.
Mohammad Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner of the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, confirmed the arrests to The Daily Star.
